newsitem.title: CHINA: China TV makers facing oversupply target exports.
newsitem.headline: China TV makers facing oversupply target exports.

text.p: China will grant its colour television makers preferential policies to help boost exports and domestic sales to relieve an industry surplus, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
China made 21 million colour televisions last year and would churn out 33 million sets in the year 2000, the newspaper quoted Chen Wenjie, an official with the State Planning Commission, as saying.
Previous figures from the Ministry of Electronics Industry show China's production capacity of colour televisions was 36 million sets last year against domestic sales of 15 million.
"The country's colour TV industry is still threatened by oversupply," the newspaper quoted Chen as saying.
Nearly 94 percent of the families in China's more affluent urban areas already own colour televisions, while some 30 percent of rural families did, Chen said.
An expected increase in domestic colour television ownership rates to 97 percent in urban areas and 40 percent in rural ones would not be enough to alleviate the oversupply, Chen said.
Authorities would help the industry boost exports to eight million sets in the year 2000 from the five million sold abroad last year, he said.
"The state will try to provide preferential policies in the fields of providing bank loans and tax collection," he said but gave no further details.
China had only a small share of the foreign television market, which was seen growing to 140 million sets in 2000, up from 110 million sets last year, he said.
Foreign markets for Chinese televisions included eastern Europe, southern Asia and South America, he said.
China made 10.44 million colour television sets in the first half of this year, an increase of 12 percent year-on-year, official figures show.
